🚨🇲🇽 <u>3,436 MORE TROOPS INTO SINALOA</u>

Mexico's federal Security Cabinet — Harfuch, Defense, Navy and the National Guard — deployed 3,436 additional troops to Mazatlán and its highways, on top of the 20,000-plus federal forces already in Sinaloa. The reinforcement: 1,600 Army, 1,000 Navy, 836 police and 100 special forces, agreed with the state's interim governor.

🇲🇽🕊️ <u>190,000 SIGNATURES FOR A DIGNIFIED DEATH</u>

Mexico's Human Rights Commission (CNDH) formally received "Ley Trasciende," a citizen initiative for the right to end life without suffering for the terminally and chronically ill — backed by roughly 190,000 signatures gathered by the Muerte Digna ¡Ya! coalition. CNDH president Rosario Piedra pledged to keep "open spaces for listening, dialogue and participation."

🇲🇽🏭 <u>A MORENA GOVERNOR SAYS THE QUIET PART</u>

Baja California Sur's Morena governor Víctor Castro proposed that the Mexican state take back the banks and shipping lines privatized in the neoliberal decades. Party boss Ricardo Monreal recoiled — "I don't believe in abrupt statization" — and the business chambers cried property rights. But Mexico has done this before: the banks in 1982, oil in 1938.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>4T UNSEALS THE ADMIRALS' BOOKS</u>

Mexico's Anti-Corruption Secretariat declassified the asset declarations of 69 active and 9 former Navy officials — filings the old regime had sealed under "national security" until 2030. Ex-Navy chief Rafael Ojeda's now-public record: 2.04 million pesos a year from his post, no real estate, a 2009 SUV, and two mortgages.

🇲🇽🌎 "Nobody decides for Mexico but Mexicans. Nobody." "Then the United States invaded us and took more than half our territory... In 1914 U.S. troops landed in Veracruz to invade us again. But the people of Mexico always fought for their independence." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, "Honestidad y Resultados," Guanajuato, Sept 18, 2026 In the cradle of Mexico's independence, Sheinbaum traced two centuries of foreign invasions back to Morelos's principle: "sovereignty emanates from the people."

🇲🇽✊ 39 years: 29,000 hospital beds. The next 36 neoliberal years: 4,000. "From 1943 to 1982, 29,000 beds were built in 39 years. Over the next 36 years, only 4,000. Now, in 12 years, we will build 9,000." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Sept 18, 2026 Health spending rises 11% this year. Sheinbaum framed the hospital-bed shortage as the inheritance of the neoliberal era — and the 4T's task to reverse.

🇲🇽🌎 "Everything possible — within our sovereignty, with respect, and for the good of Mexico." "What we are asking is the preservation of the treaty... and that the tariffs on steel, aluminum and automobiles come down, so they stop hurting these sectors of the economy." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Sept 18, 2026 Sheinbaum spoke with President Trump on Wednesday — her 22nd call with him since taking office. Talks continue; no closed deal yet.

🚨🇲🇽 Sheinbaum confirms open differences with Washington over CIA agents operating in Mexico. "In the case of Chihuahua, we've had very significant differences related to the participation of CIA agents in an operation. The Attorney General's Office even opened an investigation into it." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Sept 18, 2026 Mexico's federal prosecutor opened a probe into the CIA's role in an operation in Chihuahua. Sheinbaum said the dispute won't stop federal–state coordination.
